entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
1] This petition has been filed by the petitioner under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023/under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C., 1973, for quashment of FIR bearing Crime No.398/2024 for the offence punishable under Section 376, 376(2)
(n), 294, 506 (part II) of IPC and section 3(2)(v) and 3(2)(Va) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989 registered at Police Station Malharganj District - Indore and all other consequential proceedings arising out of the said crime number.
2] It is alleged that the petitioner committed rape on the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:5997 2 MCRC-20790-2025 prosecutrix on the pretext of marriage.

3] Counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the prosecutrix was a consenting party and they were having a relationship for the last two years, and thus, it is submitted that it is a clear case of consent, and it cannot be alleged that the prosecutrix was raped on the pretext of marriage by the petitioner.
4] Counsel for the State has opposed the prayer.

5] On due consideration and on perusal of the documents filed on record and looking to the copy of the FIR as also the charges framed, this Court Deepak vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66176651/
1 is of the considered opinion that whether the petitioner's intention was dishonest right from the beginnning as the prosecutrix entered into physical relationship with him with her consent without such promise, it is a question which is to be decided by the trial Court after the evidence is led by the parties.
